name: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, Earl of Lytton (Owen Meredith)
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, first Earl of Lytton (1831–1891), was a British statesman and poet who wrote under the pseudonym Owen Meredith. He served as Viceroy of India from 1876 to 1880.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: The Chess-Board
poems.author: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, Earl of Lytton (Owen Meredith)
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Irene, do you yet remember
Ere we were grown so sadly wise,
Those evenings in the bleak December,
Curtain'd warm from the snowy weather,
When you and I play'd chess together,
Checkmated by each other's eyes?
Ah, still I see your soft white hand
Hovering warm o'er Queen and Knight,
Brave Pawns in valiant battle stand:
The double Castles guard the wings:
The Bishop, bent on distant things,
Moves, sidling, through the fight,

Our fingers touch; our glances meet,
And falter; falls your golden hair
Against my cheek; your bosom sweet
Is heaving. Down the field, your Queen
Rides slow her soldiery all between,
And checks me unaware.
Ah me! the little battle's done,
Disperst is all its chivalry;
Full many a move, since then, have we
'Mid Life's perplexing chequers made,
And many a game with Fortune play'd, —
What is it we have won?

This, this at least — if this alone; —
That never, never, never more,
As in those old still nights of yore,
(Ere we were grown so sadly wise)
Can you and I shut out the skies,
Shut out the world, and wintry weather,
And, eyes exchanging warmth with eyes,
Play chess, as then we play'd, together!

poems.title: Tempora Acta
poems.author: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, Earl of Lytton (Owen Meredith)
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
O for the times which were (if any
Time be heroic) heroic indeed!
When the men were few,
And the deeds to do
Were mighty and many,

And each man in his hand held a noble deed.
Now the deeds are few,
And the men are many,
And each man has, at most, but a noble need.

poems.title: The Last Wish
poems.author: Robert Bulwer-Lytton, Earl of Lytton (Owen Meredith)
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
Since all that I can ever do for thee
Is to do nothing, this my prayer must be:
That thou mayst never guess nor ever see
The all-endured this nothing-done costs me.
